title: Jellyfish
titleCn: 水母种类课堂展示：煎蛋水母与黑海刺水母

paragraphs.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-six.
Hello. So we need to talk about our presentation on jellyfish. How do you think we should start?
Well, I think we should capture our audience's attention by talking about some of the strange and wonderful jellyfish species that exist.
Yeah. Good idea.
Have you heard of the fried egg jellyfish?
No.
They actually do look like an egg that's been cracked into the water.
But not as tasty, though. Are they venomous?

Yeah, but their venom has very little effect on humans and other animals. In fact, sometimes juvenile fish and crabs hide inside the jellyfish's tentacles. Fried egg jellyfish only have a lifespan of about six months, though, which isn't very long. They die in winter when the water cools down.
How about the white-spotted jellyfish?
It lives in warmer waters around the Gulf of Mexico, right?

Yeah, among other places. It has a huge appetite for some types of shrimp, fish, and crabs. It's a good example of a jellyfish that is a problem in some areas because it could destroy the populations of these creatures. It's visually striking, though.
Have you seen the bloody belly comb jellyfish?
No. Great name, though.
Yeah. It has a brilliant red stomach which actually absorbs light far below the ocean surface where they live. So they basically can't be seen by any potential predators.
Really?
They're really cool. We only really know about them because of recent studies being done in a few aquariums.
I'd like to include the black sea nettle. Did you know they have tentacles up to seven meters long?
Wow! I wouldn't like to run into one in the ocean.
[laughs] Me neither. They've only been observed in the ocean a few times but in large numbers. Swarms have been seen off the coast of California, but the sightings were decades apart.
What about the flower hat jellyfish?
They're really beautiful, aren't they?
Yeah, but people shouldn't swim near them. They have a nasty sting, which is painful and leaves a rash.
Wonder why they need such powerful venom.
It's a mystery. They only feed on tiny fish.
That is strange. Let's also look at the Atolla jellyfish.
What's special about that one?
When it's attacked, it creates very bright blue flashes that spin, kind of like on a police car.
This draws in more predators who hopefully will be interested more in the original attacker than the jellyfish, giving the jellyfish an opportunity to escape.
Wow! That's cool.
Yeah, I know.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-seven to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-seven to thirty.
For the main part of our presentation, we're going to focus on jellyfish blooms. We should define that first.
Sure.
How about a jellyfish bloom is basically when hundreds or thousands of jellyfish come together to create a giant swarm.
That's good.
We should first talk about the causes of jellyfish blooms.
It's well known that jellyfish are starting to emerge in greater numbers because fish are disappearing.
Yeah, through overfishing. And of course, another cause is chemicals from agriculture. They can flow into coastal waters and create areas of low oxygen.
Jellyfish tolerate these conditions better than fish, apparently, but I'd like to look into it more.
Yeah, me too. We also need to cite climate change as a main cause.
Sure.
Did you see the recent documentary on the Nomura jellyfish, which has appeared in large blooms off the coast of western Japan?
Yeah.
I really felt sorry for the communities who live in some of those coastal towns. When the Nomura blooms appear, they basically can't take their boats out.
It must be awful for the fishermen who've been there for generations.
I know. And it's hard to see how the issue can be dealt with long term.
Hmm. So in terms of future research, what do you think jellyfish researchers should be focusing on?
I really think that they need to do long-term studies measuring how many jellyfish there actually are in the oceans so that we can start to figure out how to deal with blooms.
I agree. Rather than looking for fossils or spending lots of time in aquariums studying how they breed.
Uh-huh.
So what do you think we should include in the handout for our presentation?
I was thinking we should include a few possible issues related to jellyfish for the class to talk about with each other in groups.

I agree, but I think we should put those up on the screen and talk about them one by one. I think it could be a good idea to use our handout to direct our classmates to some of the good online resources that are available.
Yeah. Okay.
I think they'd find that useful.
We don't want to give them too much extra reading on top of the required readings we have to do for our course.
Great. So how about we now...
That is the end of part three.
